title: It's How You Ask: Gender-Associated Linguistic Bias in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.13328v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Professional communication is increasingly mediated by LLMs - but do these models serve all users equally? We show that when prompts contain linguistic features more commonly used by women (hedges, tag questions, collective reference), they systematically elicit shorter, less sophisticated, and less formal responses across three document types and four models. These effects persist after controlling for prompt complexity and feature carry-over. Explicit gender cues like sign-off names are encoded in the same representational space as linguistic dialect - suggesting shared underlying mechanisms - yet linguistic register is far more influential, producing large, consistent effects where names produce none. translated_title: 关键在于你如何提问：大语言模型中与性别相关的语言偏见
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13328v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：专业沟通日益由大语言模型（LLMs）中介——但这些模型是否平等地服务所有用户？我们表明，当提示中包含女性更常使用的语言特征（如犹豫词、附加疑问句、集体指称）时，这些模型在三种文档类型和四种模型中系统性地产生更短、更不复杂且更不正式的回答。在控制提示复杂性和特征延续性后，这些效应依然存在。显性性别线索（如签名名称）与语言方言编码在相同的表征空间中——这表明存在共享的底层机制——然而语言语域的影响力要大得多，产生大而一致的效应，而名称则不产生任何效应。我们的结果进一步揭示，事后缓解措施具有挑战性：由于这些模式是文化嵌入的且不受意识控制，用户无法通过策略性自我呈现轻易避免它们，且机械分析也难以解决。
tldr: 本论文发现，大语言模型对女性常用语言风格（如犹豫词和附加疑问句）会产生系统性偏见，导致生成更短、更不正式的回答，且这种偏见难以通过事后缓解或用户策略规避。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that LLMs exhibit systematic bias against female-associated linguistic styles (e.g., hedges and tag questions), generating shorter and less formal responses, and this bias is difficult to mitigate post-hoc or avoid through user strategies.
